text: We tested weak-to-strong generalization using averaged labels from an ensemble of three weak supervisors (gpt2-small) to finetune a stronger student (llama-3.1-8b). The weak supervisors reach 0.6 accuracy and the strong model's ceiling performance is 0.84. Training on the ensemble-averaged labels yields a transfer accuracy of 0.74 (SE 0.01) and a performance gap recovered (PGR) of 0.59 (SE 0.04), compared with a baseline PGR of 0.4. Only two seeds (num_seeds = 2) were run, so the standard errors rest on a very small sample and should be read with caution; with this few replicates we cannot characterize run-to-run variability or rule out that seed selection drives the observed gap relative to the baseline. The direction of the result is encouraging for label averaging as a weak supervision aggregation strategy, but confirming it would require substantially more seeds, and ideally variation in ensemble size and in the weak and strong model pairing.
